item.title: Protest planned in Leverington over asylum seeker hostel proposal
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Protest planned in Leverington over asylum seeker hostel proposal
A peaceful protest is scheduled for this Sunday in Leverington regarding government plans to use Roman Court as a hostel for asylum seekers. Organised by Reform county councillor Chris Tirrell, the gathering will begin at noon at Troughton Way. The proposal aims to house 26 women and children at the site, as part of a wider plan to accommodate 205 asylum seekers across the Fenland district.
Both the local district council and MP Steve Barclay have expressed opposition to the move. A final decision on the future of the Roman Court site is expected from the government by October 16.

item.title: Police appeal for witnesses following King's Lynn collision
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Police appeal for witnesses following King's Lynn collision
Police are appealing for information following a collision at the Southgates roundabout in King's Lynn last Thursday morning. The incident occurred shortly before 6:30am and involved a white BMW and a motorbike. The motorcyclist was taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital with a broken wrist and ankle injuries.
A man in his 40s was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and driving while disqualified. He has been released on bail until November 24 while investigations continue. Officers are asking anyone with dashcam footage from the area at the time of the collision to come forward.

item.description:

Top ratings for West Norfolk leisure centres
Four council-run leisure centres in West Norfolk have been awarded a ‘very good’ rating following a national quality assessment. The sites, managed by Alive West Norfolk, include Lynnsport and St James’ Pool in King’s Lynn, Downham Leisure, and The Oasis in Hunstanton.
The Quest for Facilities scheme evaluated the centres through mystery visits and independent inspections, focusing on areas such as customer service, safety, and community engagement. In addition to this rating, the service has also received The Active Standard certification from the trade body ukactive. Council officials have praised the staff for their ongoing commitment to maintaining high standards across all four facilities.

Drivers in Wisbech are being warned of a lengthy road closure starting next month. Norwich Road will be shut to all vehicles between Churchill Road and Bowthorpe Road from October 5 until December 18. Cadent Gas Ltd is carrying out the work to replace old pipes with new plastic infrastructure.

The company says some residents may experience temporary gas supply interruptions and that site teams will provide further information to those affected.

Norfolk County Council outlines budget plans to tackle £36 million shortfall
Norfolk County Council has unveiled initial budget proposals for the 2027–28 financial year as it works to close a budget gap of nearly £36 million. Cabinet members are set to discuss the draft plans on Monday, October 5, which include over £32 million in identified savings and service efficiencies.
The proposals feature measures to support adults and families, alongside a review of council tax options. Officials describe the current financial position as challenging due to rising demand for services. If approved, the council will begin a public consultation later this month. A final decision on the budget and council tax rates is expected in February 2027, following further updates on government funding.

Half-century milestone for Ely pub regular
A long-standing patron of an Ely pub is celebrating a significant personal milestone. After initially stepping in to help out for just ten minutes, the individual has now spent fifty years working behind the bar. The long-term commitment began with a brief favour and has since turned into a half-century career at the establishment.

Three people injured following incident in Spalding
Three people have sustained injuries following an outbreak of violence in the Lincolnshire market town of Spalding. Details regarding the circumstances of the incident remain limited at this stage. Local authorities are currently managing the situation following the reports of the altercation. We will bring you further updates on this story as more information becomes available.
